newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank ensures options are open on repo rate.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank ensures options are open on repo rate.

text.p: Financial markets players were slightly surprised on Thursday to see the Bundesbank fixing its repurchase rate at 3.0 percent for just two weeks, and not for the whole of its four-week holiday period.

The Bundesbank council, which met on Thursday for the last time before a four-week summer break, said it was setting the next two repos at an unchanged 3.0 percent, meaning another decision must be made in the middle of the holiday break.
"They are leaving the possibility open, just in case something happens in the next few weeks to which they might have to react," said a money market trader based in Frankfurt.

Before this week's meeting, there had been some market speculation the central bank might move to a variable repo rate or even tighten monetary conditions in a bid to counter any possible inflationary effects of a sharply weaker currency.
With the mark currently coming in for daily beatings from the dollar, analysts said the central bank was being careful not to close off any valves.
"The bank may be on holiday for the next few weeks, but it doesn't mean that they can't make a new decision," the trader said.
